## Needs your decision: should the upload-link page say which record and field the file goes to? (#32712 item b)

Item (a) of this card is done: PR #32891 (merged) serves the page in the request's language. Item (b) asks a question first: should the page name the record and the field? Its answer decides whether a second small PR follows.

## 维护者速读

一个用户请 AI 建了 3 张报销单，拿到 3 个上传链接，在手机上逐个打开。今天这 3 个页面一字不差，只写「有一个文件要放进一条记录」，所以照片传错单、或者 AI 自己把链接绑错单，人在页面上都看不出来。单文件字段还会直接覆盖原来的文件。推荐 B′：页面多两行，例如「记录　报销单「出租车 11-12」」「放入　「发票」字段」。名字按打开页面的本人此刻能读到的样子显示，读不到就退回到只写对象名，从不显示记录编号或 API 名。别人点开同一个链接，仍然看到今天的 404 或 401，不会多看到一个字。成本是 service-storage 里一个小 PR，不改 spec。

## Why the page names nothing today

The first build of #30892 (PR #31009) let anyone holding the link use it, and a link travels: it can be forwarded or screenshotted. "Names nothing" protected the record from whoever ended up holding it. The sign-in ruling on #30892 (comment 6691366983) then changed the link. Now only the signed-in user it was made for can open the page. Anyone else, including a signed-in colleague in the same workspace, gets the same 404 as a used or expired link, and a request with no session gets a 401. The "names nothing" rule stayed, and its stated reason was reworded to "what the link is for is the agent's to say". That ruling covered sign-in only. No one has ruled on naming, so this decision does not reverse a maintainer ruling.

## Options

| | What the person sees | Privacy | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Keep "names nothing", close (b)** | Every link page reads the same: a file is wanted for a record. The agent's chat message is the only place that says which record. | Nothing about the record is shown, even to its owner. | None. |
| **B′ (recommended). Name the record and field for the link's own user** | Two extra rows: `Record  Expense "Taxi 11-12"`, `Goes into  the "Receipt" field` (or `Attachments`). The name is read as the user at page-open time. If they can no longer read the record, they get the same 404. If the title field is hidden by field-level security, masked or empty, the page shows the object label only (`Record  Expense`). If nothing can be read, the page shows today's sentence. It never shows an id, an API name, a user or an organization. The browser tab title stays generic, so the record name stays out of history. | Only the user the link was made for sees the name, and only what they can already read in the app. A forwarded link still shows nothing. The remaining exposure is someone looking at that user's screen, the same as the app itself. | One small PR in `service-storage`: read the record as the user when the page opens, the display field, the localized object and field labels, about 4–5 short strings in each of 11 languages, tests flipped from "names nothing" to "names for the owner". No spec or contract change. |
| **C. Object and field labels only** (`Expense · Receipt`) | Tells an expense apart from a contract. Three expense links still look identical. | Shows no record data. | About 60% of B′ (reviewer's estimate), because the label lookups and translations are the same work. |

## Why B′ over A and C

- **It catches a mistake while it can still be fixed.** An AI-initiated write has one human step: the person picks the file. If the agent binds the wrong record among several it just created, or the person opens the wrong link, the page under A cannot show it. For a single-file field the upload replaces the file already there, the link works once, and the page has no undo.
- **The privacy reason for A is gone.** Sign-in plus same-user already keeps the name from anyone who is not the record's reader. B′ shows that reader only what the console shows them.
- **It matches the platform's own rule.** A page or message that has a reader names the record by its title, as that reader may read it (approval notifications, #26181 A′; the record-lock sentence, #18153). A page with no reader names it by id (approval action-link pages, #23594). This page has a reader.
- **C does not help the common case.** A batch of invoices means the same object and field on every page.

**Urgency:** unmeasured. There is no customer report. The trigger is the QA finding on #32684 item 3. Priority stays p2.

## Two things this surfaced (not part of this decision)

1. A signed-out phone browser gets a raw JSON 401 with no way to sign in. For the phone scenario this blocks more than naming does. No card exists yet.
2. An upload into a single-file field silently replaces the existing file.

The seat proposes filing cards for both if you agree.

## Please pick

- **A**: close item (b) as decided; the page keeps naming nothing.
- **B′**: a follow-up PR names the record and field as above (recommended).
- **C**: a follow-up PR names the object and field labels only.

An independent review of these options, with the file and line references it checked, agrees with B′.

## Re-seen in a zh-CN deployment, plus one point the card does not name: the expiry is printed in GMT · 2026-11-13T03:06Z

Seen today on the `os-dev-test` environment: a third-party agent issued `create_upload_link` for a **line-item** file field (`c982_expense_item.invoice`, an invoice per expense line) and the user opened it in a zh-CN browser. The page is still English throughout ("Upload a file / A file was asked for, to be put in a file field of a record. Pick one and send it. This link works once. / File / Send / Uploading…"), and it does not say which claim or which line the invoice goes to — with two links for two lines open side by side, nothing on either page tells them apart.

New point: the expiry line reads **"It stops working at Fri, 13 Nov 2026 03:05:58 GMT."** For a user in UTC+8 that is 11:05 local time; printed in GMT it reads as a time hours in the past, in a language they did not choose. The localized page should state the expiry in the reader's own time zone (or as "in N minutes"), not as an RFC-1123 GMT string.

## Follow-up: both links expired before the user got to them, and the page only said so after the upload · 2026-11-13T03:07Z

Continuing the case in my previous comment (an agent issued two upload links for two expense lines). The user opened the second link, picked the PDF and pressed **Send**; the page answered with the one shared refusal:

> This upload link cannot be used: it was used already, it has expired, it was made for someone else, or it does not exist. Ask for a new link.

The page had itself printed "It stops working at … 03:06:03 GMT" when it was opened, and Send was pressed after that moment — so it was the expiry, but the user could not tell which of the four it was.

Two points, neither asking to weaken the deliberate one-answer refusal on the server (`upload-link-wire.ts`, so a link reveals nothing about which case applies):

1. **The page can say "expired" without any new disclosure.** It already rendered `expiresAt` (`upload-link-page.ts`:101). A client-side check of that same timestamp before sending — "This link expired at 11:06 (your time). Ask for a new one." — tells the reader nothing the page had not already shown, and saves picking and uploading a file into a dead link. Same for disabling Send once the printed time has passed.
2. **Ten minutes is tight for an agent hand-off.** `UPLOAD_LINK_TTL_SECONDS = 10 * 60` (`record-file-access.ts`:105). In the agent flow the agent mints the links in one turn and the person acts on them later; here both links (issued a second apart, one per line item) had expired by the time the user switched to the browser. Whether the lifetime should be longer, or configurable per deployment, is a call for the owner of this card — noting the measured case.
